title: flowmap installs into any repo as a Claude Code plugin
intent: Make flowmap easy to use on other repos: installable with two /plugin commands instead of a clone and hand-copied skills.
delta: No flow, step or call edge moves: the CLI is untouched. What changes is how the tools reach another repo. The repo now serves as its own plugin marketplace, and the two skills call `flowmap` from PATH, where the plugin's bin/ lives, instead of from a placeholder path. Change pages and the atlas also get a rendered URL on GitHub Pages, since GitHub shows committed HTML as source.

chapters.title: The repo is its own plugin marketplace
chapters.before: plugin.json existed, but with no marketplace there was no install command; the README said to copy skills/* by hand.
chapters.after: `/plugin marketplace add NelisVerhoef/flowmap` then `/plugin install flowmap@flowmap` installs both skills and puts bin/flowmap on the Bash PATH while enabled. `claude plugin validate .` passes.
chapters.claim: Any repo can get flowmap in two commands.
chapters.why: Every other repo reaches the build and review flows through this. Installs track the default branch, so it does nothing until merged.

questions.q: Should the marketplace entry pin a version or tag, so a push to main doesn't change every installed copy at once?
questions.why: Decides whether users get updates continuously or by release.

questions.q: The marketplace and plugin are both named `flowmap`, so installs read `flowmap@flowmap`. Keep that, or name the marketplace after the owner?
questions.why: The name is hard to change once people have it in their settings.

chapters.title: Flowmap pages render on GitHub Pages
chapters.before: Change pages and the atlas were committed as .html, which GitHub shows as source; a reviewer had to download one to read it.
chapters.after: On every push that touches docs/flowmap, a workflow copies changes/*.html (any branch) and atlas.html (default branch) to gh-pages, at https://nelisverhoef.github.io/Flowmap/changes/<name>.html. CLAUDE.md asks every PR to link its page there.
chapters.claim: Every PR's flowmap has a URL a reviewer can open.
chapters.why: The change page is the review entry point; if it doesn't open, reviewers fall back to reading the diff. Needs Pages turned on once (Settings → Pages → gh-pages).

questions.q: Change pages from every branch land in one flat changes/ folder, so a stale branch can overwrite pr-N.html. Fine given pages are named per PR, or key them by branch?
questions.why: Decides whether two branches can collide.

questions.q: Pages are public even if the repo later goes private on a plan without private Pages. OK for maps of private repos that copy this workflow?
questions.why: The map names every endpoint and handler.

chapters.title: The skills run flowmap from PATH
chapters.before: The skills told the agent to run `<plugin root>/bin/flowmap` or `python3 <flowmap>/bin/flowmap`, placeholders it had to resolve by guessing.
chapters.after: They run bare `flowmap`, falling back to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/flowmap` when the command isn't found.
chapters.claim: An agent following either skill no longer has to find the tool.
chapters.why: Every map build and PR lens run through an agent starts with this line; a wrong path fails the first command.

questions.q: When the skills are copied into .claude/skills instead of installed, neither PATH nor CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is set. Is the README's manual route (put bin/ on PATH) enough of a fallback?
questions.why: Decides whether the skills need a third fallback.

chapters.title: The README documents three install routes
chapters.before: One line: install the plugin from this repo, or copy skills/*.
chapters.after: Plugin install commands; a .claude/settings.json snippet (extraKnownMarketplaces + enabledPlugins) so teammates are offered the plugin when they open a repo; and a manual route.
chapters.claim: A team can adopt flowmap by committing one settings file.
chapters.why: This is what makes it spread across repos without each person installing it by hand.

questions.q: The settings snippet hasn't been tried end to end. Try it in one repo once this is merged, before recommending it to a team.
questions.why: Decides whether the team route is documented as working.
